items.text: CLI behavior and exit codes.
Case-insensitive file extensions.
Missing-file warnings.
Stable CLI/file/line precedence.
Namespace escaping and strict references.
Legacy and explicit wildcard captures.
Fixed-point expansion and expansion limits.
Strict output-prefix matching.
Typed scalar references, canonical and unique format-agnostic reference addressing, ambiguity errors, and string concatenation.
Winning-source mapping order and logical-path comment movement across overrides.
Sequence concatenation across every input format.
YAML wildcard enrichment across files.
YAML comment input and output.
JSON strict parsing and absence of comments.
XML DTD rejection and external-resource prohibition.
XML namespaces, attributes, text, mixed content, comments, CDATA, and whitespace modes.
Cross-format metadata-loss warnings.
Every scheme directive and deprecated alias.
Source-order scheme precedence, including wildcard then specific and specific then wildcard.
Negative `output=ignore`.
Uniform `root`.
Output-neutral `key`.
Locale-independent scalar inference.
JSON, YAML, and XML input structural merge.
Array concatenation, explicit-index patching, and input `merge=replace`.
Deterministic same-path `filemerge` and cross-format complete-plan overrides.
Portable shell quoting and invalid identifiers.
The documented INI dialect against representative parsers.
Output-root path confinement, including symlink or reparse-point escape attempts.
Global semantic/serialization validation gate and deterministic direct publication.
Byte-identical repeated runs under different thread schedules and locales.

Complexity bounds expressed in `N`, `P`, `E`, `M`, `C`, `G`, and `B`, verified through deterministic instrumentation of node visits, candidate checks, reference-edge visits, and produced bytes rather than wall-clock thresholds.
Scalar-plus-descendant overlays across namespace, JSON, YAML, XML, and INI.
Permanent ignore masks across concrete input, wildcard generation, references, selectors, and comments.
Stable ordering-value matching after cross-file concatenation.
Concrete output-instance expansion and wildcard default filenames.
`RestrictedYaml1` scalar and key behavior.
XML canonical addresses for namespaces, attributes, repeated children, and mixed content.
XML singleton-versus-sequence merge classification across three or more contributions.
Complete output-option replacement and contradictory flag errors.
Flat-key collision detection after delimiter and shell-identifier normalization.
Namespace multiline escape round trips.
UTF BOM handling, LF output, no output BOM, and deterministic diagnostic ordering.
Direct-publication external failure behavior without rollback.
Empty output-plan warnings and inferred-sequence compatibility warnings.
Scalar-only references and rejection of subtree and free-wildcard references.
Native sequence concatenation versus explicit ordering-value override.
Stable ordering values across deletion, wildcard matching, references, and final dense rendering.
One concrete output instance per last-wildcard capture tuple, never per descendant.
Output-instance-scoped scheme overrides and `output=ignore` restoration.
Substituted relative subfolders, encoded captures, and rejection of every `..` segment.
INI global-key preamble hoisting and rooted-section behavior.
Final fixed-point numeric-map inference, including empty mappings and generated or ignored nonnumeric children.
`type=mapping` preservation of numeric mapping keys and `type=array` conversion of nonnumeric mappings.
Deterministic multiple-capture partitioning and literal capture insertion.
Bare-scalar output behavior for every format.
Output-option defaults, XML declaration control, and comment-option enablement.
Deterministic distinct-destination publication order under partial storage failure.
Single-pass native decoded-string escaping for adjacent backslashes, wildcards, and reference starts.
JSON `EscapeNonAscii` for keys, BMP values, and supplementary Unicode scalars.
`--help`, `--version`, and every verbosity threshold without changing processing or exit status.
Fixed two-space YAML indentation, block-scalar indentation, and type-preserving string quoting.
XML comment exclusion from reference aliases and whole-element replacement under both input `merge=replace` and destination `filemerge=replace`.
Portable filename device-name handling, ASCII-case-insensitive destination collision detection, and cross-format high-water reset identically on every platform.
Namespace record classification, malformed no-`=` records, literal ordinary-value `*`, and Unicode-scalar escape validation.
INI path-to-section/key projection, namespace-only delimiter disambiguation, and `FLAT001` collisions.
Scheme-reference filename separators as encoded data, empty directive rejection, and `type=array` plus `key` rejection.
Output-instance-scoped `WARN010` suppression by `type=mapping` and stable diagnostic stream/code behavior.
Differential compatibility fixtures against namespace2xml 2.4.0 for every behavior claimed in Section 3.1, with explicit expected divergences for every correction in Section 3.2.
XML sequence projection for mapping children, root sequences, scalar items, record items, and illegal attribute projection.
Typed XML component recognition in namespace input, variables, scheme paths, references, and `root`, with literal JSON/YAML marker-shaped keys.
Deterministic global-budget attribution under varied parser thread schedules.
Phase-local diagnostic collection, complete failed-source discard, and phase-boundary abort.
Informational-mode precedence, repeated list options, `--`, and explicit-filename extension behavior.
Empty concrete output views and wildcard declarations producing no concrete instance.
`multiline` on lone scalars, empty sequences, scalar/null sequences, mappings, and container-only items.
INI simultaneous scalar-key and descendant-section projection.
XML singleton-to-sequence promotion without implicit reference or directive retargeting.
Generated `key` string typing and comment movement.
The conformance fixture layout, diagnostic-code mapping, and grammar appendices.

`--diagnostics-format` pre-scan resolution, covering `--` termination, the `=value` form, repeated occurrences, a missing value, an unrecognized value, and reporting the resulting `CLI001` in the resolved encoding.

`json` diagnostic-stream framing and closed-schema conformance, standard-error purity with operational messages suppressed, `[]` under `--verbosity none`, and a single emitted array that still contains late `PATH002` publication diagnostics.
Per-occurrence `phase` and `spec` fields for codes that arise in more than one phase.
XML attribute-count limits, absence of any separate entity-expansion budget, and deterministic `LIMIT001` attribution when per-source and global bounds are crossed together.
`--version` contract-bundle reporting and machine-readable field layout, and registry agreement with the Section 22 code-level facts.
